newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber-Prices seen steady on possible China deal.
newsitem.headline: Rubber-Prices seen steady on possible China deal.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures prices are likely to be steady this week, helped by market talk that China will buy rubber from Japanese trade houses and expectations the yen will remain weak against the dollar, traders said on Wednesday.

There was market talk that some Japanese traders had signed a contract with China to export a combined 1,200 tonnes of Ribbed Smoked Sheet (RSS) grade rubber, probably for May shipment, but this could not be immediately confirmed.
"It is believed that China will buy rubber from Japan, as Japanese rubber prices are lower relative to Thai rubber offer prices," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
"A deal could help provide support to the rubber futures markets, but would not be enough to boost prices sharply, given ample domestic rubber stocks of more than 40,000 tonnes," the analyst said.

The benchmark October rubber futures contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the Wednesday morning session at 137.6 yen per kg, down from the Monday close of 138.9 yen. The market was shut on Tuesday due to Japan's "Golden Week" holiday.
Benchmark October on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was also weaker, standing at 139.3 yen per kg at midday after closing at 140.2 yen on Monday.
Traders said that China was expected to buy more rubber from Japan if nearby rubber prices on TOCOM were to fall below 130 yen.
Trade is likely to be sluggish this week amid the Golden Week holiday and because of reluctance to sell aggressively while China remains a potential buyer.
"Sellers could be cautious of selling rubber futures at the current levels, with additional rubber sales to China looming," one trading house trader said.
"But the upside will also be limited as private investors may be quick to sell when benchmark October breaks above the 140 yen level," the trader said.
Japanese rubber prices are currently low relative to overseas prices. However, the situation differed in February when TOCOM futures prices were given a temporary boost.
Trading houses are provided with an incentive to import rubber when TOCOM prices are high compared to overseas prices.
As a result of the high TOCOM prices in February, Japan's rubber imports grew sharply, leading to a build-up in domestic stockpiles.
Japan's rubber imports in March grew a sharp 26.3 percent from the same period a year earlier to 77,843 tonnes, Finance Ministry data released on Monday showed.
The offer price for Thai rubber to Japan was quoted weaker at 108 U.S. cents per kg on a FOB basis on Wednesday, against about 110 U.S. cents on April 21.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 147 per kg on Wednesday, compared with 143 yen on April 21.
